work.title: The Life of King Henry the Fifth
work.author: William Shakespeare

content.text: Enter Gloucester, Bedford, Exeter, Erpingham, with all his host: Salisbury and Westmorland.

lines.text: Where is the King?
lines.plainText: Where is the King

lines.text: The King himself is rode to view their battle.
lines.plainText: The King himself is rode to view their battle

lines.text: Of fighting men they have full three-score thousand.
lines.plainText: Of fighting men they have full threescore thousand

lines.text: There's five to one; besides, they all are fresh.
lines.plainText: There's five to one besides they all are fresh

lines.text: God's arm strike with us! 'tis a fearful odds.
lines.plainText: God's arm strike with us 'tis a fearful odds

lines.text: God be wi' you, princes all; I'll to my charge.
lines.plainText: God be wi' you princes all I'll to my charge

lines.text: If we no more meet till we meet in heaven,
lines.plainText: If we no more meet till we meet in heaven

lines.text: Then, joyfully, my noble Lord of Bedford,
lines.plainText: Then joyfully my noble Lord of Bedford

lines.text: My dear Lord Gloucester, and my good Lord Exeter,
lines.plainText: My dear Lord Gloucester and my good Lord Exeter

lines.text: And my kind kinsman, warriors all, adieu!
lines.plainText: And my kind kinsman warriors all adieu

lines.text: Farewell, good Salisbury, and good luck go with thee!
lines.plainText: Farewell good Salisbury and good luck go with thee

lines.text: Farewell, kind lord; fight valiantly today!
lines.plainText: Farewell kind lord fight valiantly today

lines.text: And yet I do thee wrong to mind thee of it,
lines.plainText: And yet I do thee wrong to mind thee of it

lines.text: For thou art fram'd of the firm truth of valour.
lines.plainText: For thou art fram'd of the firm truth of valour

lines.text: He is as full of valour as of kindness,
lines.plainText: He is as full of valour as of kindness

lines.text: Princely in both.
lines.plainText: Princely in both

lines.text: O that we now had here
lines.plainText: O that we now had here

lines.text: But one ten thousand of those men in England
lines.plainText: But one ten thousand of those men in England

lines.text: That do no work today!
lines.plainText: That do no work today

lines.text: What's he that wishes so?
lines.plainText: What's he that wishes so

lines.text: My cousin Westmorland? No, my fair cousin.
lines.plainText: My cousin Westmorland No my fair cousin

lines.text: If we are mark'd to die, we are enough
lines.plainText: If we are mark'd to die we are enough

lines.text: To do our country loss; and if to live,
lines.plainText: To do our country loss and if to live

lines.text: The fewer men, the greater share of honour.
lines.plainText: The fewer men the greater share of honour

lines.text: God's will! I pray thee, wish not one man more.
lines.plainText: God's will I pray thee wish not one man more

lines.text: By Jove, I am not covetous for gold,
lines.plainText: By Jove I am not covetous for gold

lines.text: Nor care I who doth feed upon my cost;
lines.plainText: Nor care I who doth feed upon my cost

lines.text: It yearns me not if men my garments wear;
lines.plainText: It yearns me not if men my garments wear

lines.text: Such outward things dwell not in my desires;
lines.plainText: Such outward things dwell not in my desires

lines.text: But if it be a sin to covet honour,
lines.plainText: But if it be a sin to covet honour

lines.text: I am the most offending soul alive.
lines.plainText: I am the most offending soul alive

lines.text: No, faith, my coz, wish not a man from England.
lines.plainText: No faith my coz wish not a man from England

lines.text: God's peace! I would not lose so great an honour
lines.plainText: God's peace I would not lose so great an honour

lines.text: As one man more, methinks, would share from me
lines.plainText: As one man more methinks would share from me

lines.text: For the best hope I have. O, do not wish one more!
lines.plainText: For the best hope I have O do not wish one more

lines.text: Rather proclaim it, Westmorland, through my host,
lines.plainText: Rather proclaim it Westmorland through my host

lines.text: That he which hath no stomach to this fight,
lines.plainText: That he which hath no stomach to this fight

lines.plainText: Let him depart His passport shall be made

lines.plainText: And crowns for convoy put into his purse

lines.plainText: We would not die in that man's company

lines.text: That fears his fellowship to die with us.
lines.plainText: That fears his fellowship to die with us

lines.text: This day is call'd the feast of Crispian.
lines.plainText: This day is call'd the feast of Crispian

lines.text: He that outlives this day, and comes safe home,
lines.plainText: He that outlives this day and comes safe home

lines.text: Will stand a tip-toe when this day is named,
lines.plainText: Will stand a tiptoe when this day is named

lines.text: And rouse him at the name of Crispian.
lines.plainText: And rouse him at the name of Crispian

lines.text: He that shall live this day, and see old age,
lines.plainText: He that shall live this day and see old age

lines.plainText: Will yearly on the vigil feast his neighbours

lines.text: And say, "Tomorrow is Saint Crispian."
lines.plainText: And say Tomorrow is Saint Crispian

lines.text: Then will he strip his sleeve and show his scars,
lines.plainText: Then will he strip his sleeve and show his scars

lines.text: And say, "These wounds I had on Crispian's day."
lines.plainText: And say These wounds I had on Crispian's day

lines.text: Old men forget; yet all shall be forgot,
lines.plainText: Old men forget yet all shall be forgot

lines.text: But he'll remember with advantages
lines.plainText: But he'll remember with advantages

lines.text: What feats he did that day. Then shall our names,
lines.plainText: What feats he did that day Then shall our names

lines.text: Familiar in his mouth as household words,
lines.plainText: Familiar in his mouth as household words

lines.text: Harry the King, Bedford, and Exeter,
lines.plainText: Harry the King Bedford and Exeter

lines.text: Warwick and Talbot, Salisbury and Gloucester,
lines.plainText: Warwick and Talbot Salisbury and Gloucester

lines.text: Be in their flowing cups freshly remembered.
lines.plainText: Be in their flowing cups freshly remembered

lines.text: This story shall the good man teach his son;
lines.plainText: This story shall the good man teach his son

lines.text: And Crispin Crispian shall ne'er go by,
lines.plainText: And Crispin Crispian shall ne'er go by

lines.text: From this day to the ending of the world,
lines.plainText: From this day to the ending of the world

lines.text: But we in it shall be remembered,
lines.plainText: But we in it shall be remembered

lines.text: We few, we happy few, we band of brothers.
lines.plainText: We few we happy few we band of brothers

lines.text: For he today that sheds his blood with me
lines.plainText: For he today that sheds his blood with me

lines.text: Shall be my brother; be he ne'er so vile,
lines.plainText: Shall be my brother be he ne'er so vile

lines.text: This day shall gentle his condition;
lines.plainText: This day shall gentle his condition

lines.text: And gentlemen in England now abed
lines.plainText: And gentlemen in England now abed

lines.text: Shall think themselves accurs'd they were not here,
lines.plainText: Shall think themselves accurs'd they were not here

lines.text: And hold their manhoods cheap whiles any speaks
lines.plainText: And hold their manhoods cheap whiles any speaks

lines.text: That fought with us upon Saint Crispin's day.
lines.plainText: That fought with us upon Saint Crispin's day

lines.text: My sovereign lord, bestow yourself with speed.
lines.plainText: My sovereign lord bestow yourself with speed

lines.text: The French are bravely in their battles set,
lines.plainText: The French are bravely in their battles set

lines.text: And will with all expedience charge on us.
lines.plainText: And will with all expedience charge on us

lines.text: All things are ready, if our minds be so.
lines.plainText: All things are ready if our minds be so

lines.text: Perish the man whose mind is backward now!
lines.plainText: Perish the man whose mind is backward now

lines.text: Thou dost not wish more help from England, coz?
lines.plainText: Thou dost not wish more help from England coz

lines.text: God's will! my liege, would you and I alone,
lines.plainText: God's will my liege would you and I alone

lines.text: Without more help, could fight this royal battle!
lines.plainText: Without more help could fight this royal battle

lines.text: Why, now thou hast unwish'd five thousand men,
lines.plainText: Why now thou hast unwish'd five thousand men

lines.text: Which likes me better than to wish us one.
lines.plainText: Which likes me better than to wish us one

lines.text: You know your places. God be with you all!
lines.plainText: You know your places God be with you all

lines.text: Once more I come to know of thee, King Harry,
lines.plainText: Once more I come to know of thee King Harry

lines.text: If for thy ransom thou wilt now compound,
lines.plainText: If for thy ransom thou wilt now compound

lines.text: Before thy most assured overthrow;
lines.plainText: Before thy most assured overthrow

lines.text: For certainly thou art so near the gulf,
lines.plainText: For certainly thou art so near the gulf

lines.plainText: Thou needs must be englutted Besides in mercy

lines.plainText: The Constable desires thee thou wilt mind

lines.text: Thy followers of repentance; that their souls
lines.plainText: Thy followers of repentance that their souls

lines.plainText: May make a peaceful and a sweet retire

lines.text: From off these fields, where, wretches, their poor bodies
lines.plainText: From off these fields where wretches their poor bodies

lines.text: Must lie and fester.
lines.plainText: Must lie and fester

lines.text: Who hath sent thee now?
lines.plainText: Who hath sent thee now

lines.text: The Constable of France.
lines.plainText: The Constable of France

lines.text: I pray thee, bear my former answer back:
lines.plainText: I pray thee bear my former answer back

lines.text: Bid them achieve me and then sell my bones.
lines.plainText: Bid them achieve me and then sell my bones

lines.plainText: Good God why should they mock poor fellows thus

lines.plainText: The man that once did sell the lion's skin

lines.plainText: While the beast liv'd was kill'd with hunting him

lines.plainText: A many of our bodies shall no doubt

lines.text: Find native graves, upon the which, I trust,
lines.plainText: Find native graves upon the which I trust

lines.text: Shall witness live in brass of this day's work;
lines.plainText: Shall witness live in brass of this day's work

lines.plainText: And those that leave their valiant bones in France

lines.plainText: Dying like men though buried in your dunghills

lines.plainText: They shall be fam'd for there the sun shall greet them

lines.plainText: And draw their honours reeking up to heaven

lines.plainText: Break out into a second course of mischief

lines.plainText: Killing in relapse of mortality

lines.plainText: Let me speak proudly tell the Constable

lines.plainText: We are but warriors for the workingday

lines.plainText: With rainy marching in the painful field

lines.plainText: And my poor soldiers tell me yet ere night

lines.plainText: The gay new coats o'er the French soldiers' heads

lines.plainText: Come thou no more for ransom gentle herald

lines.plainText: They shall have none I swear but these my joints

lines.plainText: I fear thou'lt once more come again for ransom
